title: Ivo and the Witness
premise: Ada Iversen, host of the true-crime podcast 'Cold Ledger,' has spent three years documenting the 1994 disappearance of schoolteacher Marta Voss in the fjord town of Skarvik — a case closed as an accident, statute of limitations expiring in six months. When twin letters arrive, one confessing to the crime and one promising 'the rest of the truth' if Ada investigates publicly, she is pulled into a cat-and-mouse game with someone who has read every page of her research. As Ada and her found family — retired constable Halvard, archivist June, and estranged half-sister Nell — follow the letters through Skarvik's buried complicity, they discover the confessor is not the killer but the killer's protector, and that the real murderer sits on the committee deciding whether the case reopens. In the end, Ada stages a fake statute-expiry deadline to force the killer into destroying evidence, catches him on tape, and chooses love for her fragile new family over the exclusive scoop that would have made her career.
about_author: Lior Eriksen is a former court reporter from coastal Norway who spent a decade transcribing other people's worst days before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn mysteries about small towns that keep their secrets the way harbors keep their water.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. We meet Ada mid-recording, cataloging the Marta Voss case with obsessive precision — files alphabetized, grief kept at arm's length. The episode airs; listener mail arrives, including two envelopes postmarked Skarvik. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. One letter confesses to killing Marta Voss; the second, written in the same hand, promises 'the rest' only if Ada comes to Skarvik and investigates out loud. She compares handwriting against her archive and finds it matches a 1996 witness statement. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Return to Skarvik
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada drives north to the gray harbor town, checking into the same guesthouse where Marta once lived. The town is polite, watchful, closed. Former constable Halvard Brandt recognizes her podcast voice and warns her off — then slips her his old case notebook. Beat: unease beneath hospitality.

chapters.title: The Constable's Notebook
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Flashback-tinged chapter: Halvard recounts the 1994 investigation he was ordered to close as accidental drowning by committee chair Eirik Lund. He never believed it. Now he sees Ada as his last chance at absolution. Beat: guilt seeking redemption.

chapters.title: Second Letter
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A second letter appears inside her locked car: details of Marta's last day that were never public. It instructs her to interview specific townspeople in order. June, the young town archivist, offers help and becomes Ada's first ally. Beat: the game begins; fear mixed with exhilaration.

chapters.title: Witnesses in Order
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following the letter's list, Ada interviews three aging witnesses whose stories contradict the official file in small, deliberate ways. Someone photographs her at each stop. Beat: mounting paranoia — she is being choreographed.

chapters.title: Nell
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Ada's estranged half-sister arrives uninvited; their mother was Marta's cousin, and Nell wants answers too. Their reunion is barbed — old wounds over their mother's silence about Skarvik. Nell moves into the guesthouse. Beat: friction that hints at found family.

chapters.title: The Committee
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada petitions the municipal review committee to reopen the case before the statute expires in five months. Chair Eirik Lund is charming, helpful, and quietly kills the motion on procedure. That night, a third letter praises her 'performance.' Beat: power flexing behind civility.

chapters.title: What June Found
chapters.summary: June's POV. In the archives, June discovers Marta had been auditing the harbor trust's books before she vanished — and that pages are missing from 1994. June tells only Ada. Beat: motive surfaces; corruption takes shape.

chapters.title: The Confessor
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada traces the letters' paper stock to a print shop and confronts the buyer: Torvald Ness, Marta's former colleague, who breaks down and admits writing them — but swears he only covered for someone. He won't say who. Beat: pity for a coward; the trail bends.

chapters.title: Fire at the Archive
chapters.summary: June's POV. The archive wing burns overnight; the 1994 harbor-trust ledgers are destroyed. June is hospitalized with smoke inhalation. Ada realizes the killer is protecting money, not just a secret. Beat: stakes turn physical; rage and fear.

chapters.title: Halvard Breaks
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Halvard confesses to Ada that in 1994 he saw a car near the dock the night Marta died and stayed silent because the driver was powerful. His shame nearly ends him; Ada refuses to let him resign from the fight. Beat: duty versus conscience, the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The Middle of It
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The four — Ada, Halvard, June, Nell — form an uneasy team, mapping everything they know on the guesthouse wall. They realize the letters' sequence mirrors the original investigation's order: the writer knows the case file better than the investigators did. Beat: found family coalescing around a shared table.

chapters.title: Eirik's Dinner
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Lund invites Ada to dinner, all charm, offering funding and fame if she drops the case — and a veiled threat about her mother's debts if she doesn't. Ada records nothing and says less, but leaves certain he knows what she knows. Beat: seduction of power, refused.

chapters.title: Nell's Discovery
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Going through their late mother's things, Nell finds letters showing their mother knew Marta was afraid — and was paid afterward to stay quiet. Nell must decide whether to tell Ada. Beat: loyalty tested by protective lies.

chapters.title: Torvald Runs
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Torvald panics after the fire and tries to flee; Ada and Halvard intercept him at the ferry. He gives them one name under pressure — not Lund, but Lund's fixer, dockmaster Sander Koll — then disappears into the crowd. Beat: hope with a hole in it.

chapters.title: Koll
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Halvard leans on old police contacts to pressure Koll, who admits moving Marta's body from the harbor office to the cove on Lund's orders — manslaughter turned cover-up. But Koll won't testify without proof Lund ordered the death itself. Beat: the noose tightening around the wrong neck.

chapters.title: The Trap
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. With the statute weeks away, the team leaks a false story: the case will be statutorily barred Friday, and all evidence will be sealed and destroyed Monday. Only someone who'd need to destroy physical proof would act. They stake out the boathouse where Marta's belongings were stored. Beat: cold, controlled anticipation.

chapters.title: Friday Night
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Lund comes himself, believing the seal order, and begins burning the last box — containing Marta's audit notes naming him. Halvard steps out of the dark and arrests him; June films; Koll, watching, agrees to testify. Beat: climax — power caught in the act of corrupting itself.

chapters.title: Confession, Complete
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In custody, Lund unravels: Marta confronted him over embezzlement; he struck her; Torvald helped hide it. The final letter's author is revealed — Torvald, who wanted Lund exposed but couldn't do it alone, and chose Ada because she filed the truth better than anyone. Beat: catharsis and bitter clarity.

chapters.title: The Episode
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Facing the choice between breaking the story first or letting the prosecution proceed cleanly, Ada delays her episode until after charges are filed — sacrificing the exclusive. She records the final episode with Halvard, June, and Nell beside her. Beat: love against duty, resolved in favor of love.

chapters.title: After the Thaw
chapters.summary: Ensemble epilogue, spring. Marta is reburied with her name restored; the harbor trust is dissolved; Halvard tends her grave. Ada stays in Skarvik longer than planned — the guesthouse lease renewed, the wall map finally taken down. Last line lands on the empty chair where the letters used to arrive. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
